correctness.rationale: The exact chain rule gives a triangular coefficient matrix at every homogeneous derivative order; determinant-one change of variables preserves each L1 integral. The positive binomial column sums strictly grow with derivative order for any nonzero shear, yielding the all-order upper bound. The 2017 published Ornstein theorem applies to any kth derivative monomial against the other linearly independent same-order monomials, producing tests with arbitrarily dominant chosen derivative; reverse triangle inequality and dilation give the matching lower bound. Strict positivity of zeroth-order L1 mass yields nonattainment. Exact polynomial differences yield the order-two and order-three crossover thresholds and slope discontinuities. The finite exact rational checker supports the algebra but is not substituted for Ornstein or the infinite-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The exact bounded-shear distortion in the 2026 derivative-sum Sobolev norm is not a result of the inspected motivating isometry classification, which treats norm-one surjections. The crucial availability of near-single-monomial top jets is established by the 1962/2017 Ornstein non-inequality and is explicitly not claimed new. The fresh result is the quantitative application that identifies the exact all-order affine pullback constant, nonattainment, and the two sharp order-three cusps. Closest searched literature treats qualitative isometries, different Sobolev composition regimes, or the derivative non-inequality itself; it has not been shown to imply this exact theorem without additional argument. Priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An earlier exact norm formula for affine pullbacks on this special L1 derivative-sum Sobolev space may appear under equivalent jet, differential-polynomial, or Sobolev coordinate-change terminology.
The accessible full text of the Biegert–Nittka preprint and Oliva–Prats article was not obtained, limiting exclusion of any unrelated special-case claims.

The result is a quantitative specialization using the known Ornstein non-inequality, rather than a standalone general endpoint operator theorem; priority assessment depends on whether a previous source had already made this particular synthesis.

value.rationale: The recently studied complete W^{k,1} derivative-sum norm is coordinate-sensitive, so the quantitative cost of a basic determinant-one shear is a natural invariant of the Sobolev geometry. The theorem gives the entire sharp all-order law, not an arbitrary finite sample, and resolves two genuine k=3 cusp thresholds. The small-shear sharp k=2 constant exceeds all single-direction high-frequency rank-one tests by at least 2q(1-q)/3, making the appearance of the non-inequality mathematically essential. It provides a meaningful benchmark for quantitative stability of the isometry classification while limiting claims to this natural affine family.
